questions.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
{B}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 6 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}],\,{B}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 9 \\ -6 & 0\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 8 \\ -5 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

If $B=\{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}\},$ and $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{B}_{1}+{x}_{2}{B}_{2}=A.
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}0 & 6 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 & 9 \\ -6 & 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 8 \\ -5 & 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 & 6{x}_{1}+9{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2} & 3{x}_{1}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 8 \\ -5 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}6{x}_{1}+9{x}_{2}=8 \\ -3{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=-5 \\ 3{x}_{1}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}6 & 9 & 8 \\ -3 & -6 & -5 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}6 & 9 & 8 \\ -3 & -6 & -5 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(\frac{1}{2}){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}6 & 9 & 8 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{2} & -1 \\ 0 & -\frac{9}{2} & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}6{x}_{1}+9{x}_{2}=8 \\ -\frac{3}{2}{x}_{2}=-1 \\ -\frac{9}{2}{x}_{2}=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second and third equations, we get ${x}_{2}=\frac{2}{3}.$ From the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}6{x}_{1}+9\cdot \frac{2}{3} & =8 \\ 6{x}_{1} & =2 \\ {x}_{1} & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=\frac{1}{3}+\frac{2}{3}=1.$

questions.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
{B}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 7 \\ -5 & 0\end{aligned}],\,{B}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

If $B=\{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}\},$ and $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{B}_{1}+{x}_{2}{B}_{2}=A.
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 & 7 \\ -5 & 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1} & 7{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} \\ -5{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} & 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}=-2 \\ 7{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=-1 \\ -5{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=3.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -2 \\ 7 & 3 & -1 \\ -5 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -2 \\ 7 & 3 & -1 \\ -5 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-\frac{7}{2}){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+\frac{5}{2}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}=-2 \\ 3{x}_{2}=6 \\ -{x}_{2}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second and third equations, we get ${x}_{2}=2.$ From the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=-1.$ 

Therefore, $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-1+2=1.$

questions.problem:
Consider the following polynomials:

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=-1-t+2{t}^{2},\,{p}_{2}(t)=t-{t}^{2},\,q(t)=3-3t.
$$

If $B=\{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)\},$ and $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t)=q(t)
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(-1-t+2{t}^{2})+{x}_{2}(t-{t}^{2}) & =3-3t \\ -{x}_{1}+(-{x}_{1}+{x}_{2})t+(2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}){t}^{2} & =3-3t.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}=3 \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-3 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & -1 & 6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}=3 \\ {x}_{2}=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

From the first and second equations, we get ${x}_{1}=-3$ and ${x}_{2}=-6.$ 

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -6\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-3+(-6)=-9.$

questions.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
{B}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{B}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

If $B=\{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}\},$ and $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{B}_{1}+{x}_{2}{B}_{2}=A.
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & -2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ 0 & {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=6 \\ -{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-2 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 6 \\ -1 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 6 \\ -1 & 1 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=6 \\ {x}_{2}=4 \\ -{x}_{2}=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

 
From the second and third equations, we get ${x}_{2}=4.$ From the first equation, we get  ${x}_{1}=6.$

Therefore, $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=6+4=10.$

questions.problem:
Consider the following polynomials:

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=2-t,\,{p}_{2}(t)=3-2{t}^{2},\,q(t)=3t-4{t}^{2}.
$$

If $B=\{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)\},$ and $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t)=q(t)
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(2-t)+{x}_{2}(3-2{t}^{2}) & =3t-4{t}^{2} \\ (2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2})-{x}_{1}t-2{x}_{2}{t}^{2} & =3t-4{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0 \\ -{x}_{1}=3 \\ -2{x}_{2}=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}=3 \\ 3{x}_{2}=6 \\ -2{x}_{2}=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second and third equations we get ${x}_{2}=2.$ From the  first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-3.$

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-3+2=-1.$
